projects.title: 10 AI Workflows That Can Save Students Hours Every Week
projects.topic: 10 practical, proven AI workflows that help students and young professionals automate study notes, exam preparation, research synthesis, and job applications.

slides.headline: 10 AI Workflows That Save Students 15+ Hours Every Week
slides.description: Stop spending countless late nights summarizing lecture PDFs and formatting citations. Here are 10 proven workflows that turn AI into your highest-leverage study partner.

slides.headline: The Core Problem: Passive Reading vs Active Synthesis
slides.description: Most students use AI as a lazy search engine. But when you treat LLMs as active Socratic sparring partners, retention triples and synthesis takes minutes instead of hours.

slides.headline: Workflow 1: Socratic Lecture Sparring
slides.description: Feed your lecture transcript to Claude or ChatGPT with the prompt: 'Act as my harsh oral exam professor. Ask me one concept question at a time and grade my answers.'

slides.headline: Workflow 2: Multi-Paper Literature Synthesis
slides.description: Upload 3 foundational papers into Perplexity or NotebookLM. Ask for a comparison matrix highlighting where researchers agree, contradict each other, and leave open gaps.

slides.headline: Workflow 3: Formula Derivation Step-Back Prompting
slides.description: Never ask for the final answer. Ask: 'Guide me through the derivation of this formula using first principles, revealing one hint whenever I say CONTINUE.'

slides.headline: Workflow 4: Code Explainer with Mental Models
slides.description: Paste complex algorithmic code and ask: 'Explain this recursion using a real-world restaurant kitchen analogy. Then point out the edge case that breaks it.'

slides.headline: Workflow 5: Resume & Cover Letter Tailoring
slides.description: Map job descriptions against your verified project achievements using strict JSON diffs to spot missing keywords and weak impact verbs before submitting.

slides.headline: Practical Implementation: Build a Personal Prompt Bank
slides.description: Don't write prompts from scratch every day. Maintain a curated markdown cheat sheet in Obsidian or Notion with your top 5 calibrated system prompts.

slides.headline: Common Mistake: Blindly Trusting Unchecked Citations
slides.description: LLMs can confidently hallucinate page numbers and author years. Always verify citations using Google Scholar, PubMed, or Perplexity verified links.

slides.headline: Which workflow will you try before your next exam?
slides.description: Bookmark this carousel for your study sessions. Share it with a friend who spends too many late nights buried under lecture slides.

slides.headline: 7 AI Tools That Save 20+ Hours a Week
slides.description: Stop spending 60% of your founder hours on administrative tasks. Here is the exact stack top tech founders are using to operate as a 10-person team.

slides.headline: 1. Granola — Intelligent Meeting Synthesis
slides.description: Standard transcripts are boring. Granola takes your raw spoken notes and drafts customer PRDs, follow-up emails, and investor summaries in seconds.

slides.headline: 2. Claude 3.5 Sonnet — Strategy & Code
slides.description: Use Artifacts to prototype interactive mini-tools, analyze complex financial spreadsheets, and draft high-converting landing page copy.

slides.headline: 3. Framewise — Auto Carousel & Pitch Decks
slides.description: Turn raw thoughts into high-engagement LinkedIn and Instagram carousels with strict JSON layout guarantees and 1-click PDF export.

slides.headline: 4. Clay.com — AI Lead Enrichment
slides.description: Scrape, verify, and personalize cold outbound emails with 50+ data sources without hiring an expensive SDR team.

slides.headline: 5. Perplexity Pro — Fact-Checked Market Research
slides.description: Replace hours of generic Google browsing with cited, real-time academic and industry intelligence.

slides.headline: The Golden Rule of AI Delegation
slides.description: Never delegate thinking — delegate execution. Use AI to create the first draft and refine the structure, but keep founder judgment at the center.
